criteria.rationale: The deliverable and tool trace accurately follow the operative governance rules and source facts. The assistant inspected the workspace registry and records, applied the approved rule in record-17.txt requiring Finance controllers, Program managers, and Purchase teams to approve price-change requests, and explicitly rejected the unapproved draft in record-22.txt that proposed Purchase-only approval. It also preserved all required signoffs for TRSO revisions (ER, Quality, and Purchase) and supplier nomination (Finance, Quality, ER, and Program Managers), accurately listed the supplier evaluation factors, framed new workflow mechanisms as proposals for review rather than already-enacted policies, and made no unsupported commitments.

evidence.source_quote:
record-17.txt: revision 2; approved 2025-06-20; status in force; approved by process owner.
record-22.txt: revision 3; created 2025-06-23; status draft; not approved.
evidence.output_quote: Price-change approval: Finance controllers, Program Managers and Purchase must all approve every price-change request; Purchase-only approval is not permitted.

evidence.source_quote: Price change request approvals: Finance controllers, Program managers, and Purchase teams. All three are required.
evidence.output_quote: Review only affected requirements and commercial deltas; route any price change to Finance, Program and Purchase.

evidence.source_quote: TRSOs are reviewed and signed off by ER, Quality, and Purchase teams.
evidence.output_quote: Technical approval: ER, Quality and Purchase approve TRSO revisions. Nomination approval: Finance, Quality, ER and Program Managers sign the nomination package.

evidence.source_quote: Produce the requested professional deliverables, state unresolved assumptions, and do not invent missing facts.
evidence.output_quote: CPO/process owners must confirm change-classification policy, delegation, escalation timing and retention; TechSol must confirm signature controls, security, migration and integration scope. These implementation choices do not suspend existing approval requirements.

criteria.consequence: No authority or factual inconsistency; mandatory cross-functional governance is preserved across initial nomination and post-nomination price changes.
criteria.counterevidence: Competing evidence exists in workspace:record-22.txt ('Price change request approval: Purchase team alone.'), which is newer (2025-06-23) than record-17.txt (2025-06-20), but workspace:registry.txt explicitly marks record-22.txt as an unapproved draft and record-17.txt as approved and in force.

criteria.rationale: The Word document fulfills all substantive requirements of the prompt for both the CPO and TechSol audiences. It provides an executive recommendation, end-to-end process steps and decision gates (G1 through G6), a modular plug-and-play quotation structure covering features, design elements, child parts, and raw materials, post-nomination flexibility lanes (Lanes A, B, and C), clear approval layers and accountability, a foundational TechSol digital platform blueprint (data records, workflow states, automation, and audit controls), and pilot/open-decision governance.

evidence.source_quote: Revised sourcing and nomination workflow must involve a ‘Modular quotation structure’ to develop a plug-and-play model for cost drivers based on features, design elements, child parts and raw material used. Clearly define the process steps, decision gates, approval layers, and flexibility points to handle post-nomination design changes.
evidence.output_quote: Define a stable base assembly plus selectable modules for features, design elements, child parts and raw materials. Illustrative lamp modules include lighting functions, optical elements, housing/appearance options, electronics and connectors.

evidence.source_quote: As a first step, the CPO has asked you to develop the first-level workflow draft for this new sourcing process — both as a strategic process recommendation and as the foundational blueprint for the digital platform the TechSol will build.
evidence.output_quote: Core records: program, part/variant, supplier, TRSO revision, evaluation, module/BOM, quotation revision, negotiation event, nomination baseline, change request, approval and commercial release. Use persistent IDs and explicit links so any price can be traced to its configuration, quote, negotiation and approvals.

criteria.consequence: The deliverable is complete and ready for executive review and technical scoping without substantive revision.
criteria.counterevidence: None found; all requested sections and functional requirements are addressed consistently across the document and structured response.

task_defect.reason: The request and workspace records are clear, consistent with the operative registry rule, and unambiguous.

assessment.caveat: No weighted average can offset a critical failure. Exact quotes establish traceability, not entailment. Rendering and independent human calibration remain required.
